title: MNC consultative selling
body:
Use this playbook for enterprise and MNC accounts with sites in more than one country: Singapore-headquartered groups with plants in Johor or Bengaluru, Indian companies expanding to Singapore or Southeast Asia, and MNCs present in both India and Singapore.

## Principles

- Lead with the customer's business problem, not a product. Ask what the operation must achieve in the next 12 to 24 months, then map each gap to an outcome.
- Sell bundles across the catalogue, not single products. The catalogue has 6 core products (5G+, CUBΣ, Cyber Security, IoT, Mobility, Quantum-Safe Network) and 3 extras (RE:AI, Nxera, NCS). Nothing else is sold.
- Match the buyer type. Risk-averse buyers get certifications, track record, and risk assessments. Innovation-driven buyers get a pilot. Efficiency-driven buyers get a business case with measurable outcomes. Partnership-driven buyers get a multi-year account plan.
- Map every stakeholder by role: the economic buyer (often the Group CFO or COO), technical buyers (Group CIO, CISO), users (Head of Operations), and the champion.

## Discovery questions

1. Which sites are opening, closing, or growing in the next 18 months, and in which countries?
2. Where does traffic break out to the internet today, and who owns the security policy for each site?
3. Which workloads carry regulated data (PDPA in Singapore, the DPDP Act in India, the Malaysian PDPA in Johor), and where must that data stay?
4. Which incidents in the last 12 months cost the business money or reputation?
5. How is a multi-country contract approved, and which legal entity signs and pays?

## Account plan structure

1. Now: what the account owns, its contract end date, open incidents, and billing status.
2. Next 6 to 12 months: likely needs from signals, site plans, and pain points.
3. Bundle path: the outcome bundle that closes each gap, with indicative ARR derived from catalogue ARR, never Singtel list pricing.

## Rules

- Every claim about a company carries a source link. With no source, say "No signal found".
- SingTech drafts; the account executive approves before anything reaches the customer or is saved as final in Salesforce. Emails are never sent automatically.
- Do not compete on price cuts. Defend value with SLA, coverage, and one accountable partner.

title: Government and CII deals routed through NCS
body:
Use this playbook when the customer is a government agency, a government contractor, or an owner of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII). Singapore's Cybersecurity Act sets obligations for CII owners in sectors including aviation, maritime, banking, and energy (source: https://www.csa.gov.sg/legislation/cybersecurity-act).

## When to route through NCS

Route the Opportunity as "NCS multi-LOB" when any of these is true:

- The scope includes application, cloud, or data work for a public-sector contract.
- The customer's contract terms require in-country processing or controls that a systems integrator must evidence.
- More than one NCS line of business is needed, for example Government and Public Sector plus Cyber Security Services.

NCS is Singtel Group's technology services arm for cloud migration, application modernisation, and data engineering, and it reported record FY26 bookings of S$3.8 billion (source: https://www.telecomtv.com/content/digital-platforms-services/singtel-posts-fy26-net-profit-of-s-5-61bn-underlying-profit-up-12-to-s-2-77bn-55535/).

## Roles

- Singtel account executive: owns the relationship, the connectivity, 5G+, and Cyber Security scope, and the Salesforce Opportunity.
- NCS client director: owns the NCS lines of business and chairs the programme board.
- Each NCS line of business is a separate line item on one Opportunity, so the customer sees one proposal.

## Motion

1. Confirm the CII or government scope in writing with the customer's contracts team.
2. Run feasibility for every site. An off-net site inside a CII scope needs an explicit SLA carve-out or a build plan.
3. Agree data residency early. Private 5G with multi-access edge computing keeps processing on site; RE:AI is hosted in Singapore.
4. Hold one joint programme board with NCS and record every decision in the Chatter deal room.
5. Map the paper process on day one; government-linked contracts often need a longer legal review.

## Watch-outs

- Never present Singtel and NCS as competing bidders on the same scope.
- Do not promise compliance outcomes. The customer remains the CII owner and is accountable for its obligations.
- Sample account Meridian Arcwell Group shows the full pattern: four NCS lines of business, an operations centre with data residency terms, and off-net overseas sites.

title: Site feasibility: On-Net, Near-Net, and Off-Net routing
body:
Every proposal starts with fibre and 5G feasibility at each customer site. SingTech gives each site one status per technology.

## Statuses

- On-net: Singtel fibre or 5G coverage already reaches the building. Quote standard lead times.
- Near-net: coverage is close, but a short lateral build or indoor coverage work is needed. Add a site survey line and confirm build cost and lead time with the solution architect before quoting a go-live date.
- Off-net: no Singtel coverage. Service depends on a partner tail circuit or a new build. A partner tail is usually outside the Singtel SLA, so state the carve-out in the proposal or plan a managed alternative.

## Routing rules

1. All sites on-net: route as a standard Singtel Enterprise deal.
2. Any near-net site: add a site survey and a lead-time caveat. Do not commit a go-live date until the survey is back.
3. Any off-net site inside a CII or government scope: route through NCS with the network scope and make the SLA carve-out explicit.
4. Overseas sites (Johor, Bengaluru, Jakarta, Chennai, Mumbai): treat as off-net unless a confirmed partner path exists. For Johor, the TM Nxera campus is a candidate landing point (source: Nxera catalogue entry, https://www.itnews.asia/news/singtels-nxera-opens-58mw-data-centre-in-singapore-623491).
5. Sites with recurring strain (link saturation, slow syncs, Wi-Fi congestion) are upgrade candidates. Quote the measured strain in the proposal.
6. A site can be near-net for fibre and on-net for 5G. That combination is the strongest case for private 5G with edge processing.

## Lessons from sample accounts

- Off-net partner tails caused the Johor, Chennai, and Bengaluru incidents in the sample data, and no service credit applied. Customers notice; address it before renewal.
- Seats per site size the Mobility and security scope; strain notes size the bandwidth and 5G scope.

title: MEDDPICC qualification guide
body:
SingTech scores each account's main Opportunity on the 8 MEDDPICC elements, 0 to 2 each, for a total of 0 to 16.

## Scoring

- 0: unknown or not started.
- 1: partly known, not yet confirmed by the customer.
- 2: confirmed by the customer, with evidence recorded.

## Elements

- Metrics: the measurable outcome the customer will judge success by, such as cutting a nightly sync from 5 hours to under 30 minutes.
- Economic Buyer: the person who can release budget. Score 2 only after direct contact.
- Decision Criteria: the written criteria and their weights.
- Decision Process: the steps, people, and dates from evaluation to signature.
- Paper Process: legal, procurement, PO, and supplier onboarding steps, including the billing system that will receive the invoice.
- Identify Pain: the business pain, with numbers and a source (telemetry, an incident, or the customer's own words).
- Champion: an insider who sells for us when we are not in the room. Test a champion by asking for something only an insider can provide.
- Competition: who else is in the deal, for which scope, and how the customer sees them.

## Forecast guide

This is a SingTech planning convention, not a Singtel standard.

- 12 to 16: commit candidate.
- 8 to 11: best case; close the named gaps.
- 0 to 7: pipeline only; qualify before investing specialist time.

## Rules

- Every score needs evidence text. Every score under 2 needs a gap and a next step.
- Paper Process scores 0 while an invoice is disputed or supplier onboarding is incomplete; finance goodwill matters.
- Re-score after every customer meeting and post the change in the Chatter deal room.

title: Renewal-window upsell motion
body:
The upsell window opens 18 months before contract end and closes 12 months before it (365 to 548 days before the end date, inclusive). SingTech flags accounts inside this window.

## Why this window

Inside 12 months, the customer is in renewal mode: procurement runs a competitive check and the conversation turns to price. Between 12 and 18 months out, budget for the next cycle is still being planned, so an outcome-based bundle can be built into it.

## Motion

1. 18 months out: refresh the account plan. Confirm owned products, open incidents, billing status, and site feasibility.
2. 15 to 18 months out: run a value review with the economic buyer, using measured strain (link load, sync times, incidents) as evidence.
3. 12 to 15 months out: submit an outcome-based proposal with indicative ARR derived from catalogue ARR, plus a starter option for a smaller first step.
4. Inside 12 months: renewal defence. Clear disputed or overdue invoices, close SLA root causes, and lock the renewal before a competitive check.
5. 90 days before the end date: SingTech raises a renewal alert and drafts a Salesforce Task for the account executive to approve.

## Inputs SingTech uses

Contract end date, MEDDPICC total, open SLA incidents and credits, disputed or overdue invoices, and competitor activity.

## Rules

- Do not discount to win a renewal. Offer the starter bundle instead.
- Resolve billing disputes before the proposal reaches legal.
- As of November 2026, sample account Meridian Arcwell Group sits inside the window (contract end 30 April 2028) with a disputed invoice, SGT-INV-2026-8841, that must be cleared first.

title: Objection handling
body:
Acknowledge the concern, ask one clarifying question, answer with evidence, and confirm the next step. Never disparage a competitor and never quote competitor pricing without a source.

## "StarHub, M1, or NTT is cheaper"

- Ask what their quote covers: which sites, security controls, SLA terms, overseas coverage, and who manages partner tails.
- Compare total cost, including partner tails, separate security tooling, and the customer's in-house effort to run several vendors.
- Offer the starter bundle as a smaller first step instead of a discount. Pricing is indicative, derived from catalogue ARR.
- Lead with what one accountable partner removes: the incident hand-offs the customer already lived through.

## "Our data must stay in Singapore" or "in India"

- RE:AI is a sovereign AI cloud with GPU-as-a-Service and token-based AI services hosted in Singapore (source: https://www.re-ai.ai/about-us/newsroom/singtel-re-ai-first-in-APAC-to-deploy-nvidia-dgx-gb300).
- Nxera offers AI-ready colocation at the 58MW DC Tuas facility (source: https://www.itnews.asia/news/singtels-nxera-opens-58mw-data-centre-in-singapore-623491).
- Private 5G with multi-access edge computing keeps processing on site for CII and government scopes (source: https://www.singtel.com/business/products-services/5g).
- For India, the DPDP Act governs transfers of personal data outside India (source: https://www.meity.gov.in/data-protection-framework), and RBI rules require payment system data to be stored in India (source: https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=11244). Involve NCS for government or CII scopes.

## "Who is liable if there is a PDPA breach?"

- The customer keeps its own obligations under the PDPA as the organisation responsible for the data (source: https://www.pdpc.gov.sg/overview-of-pdpa/the-legislation/personal-data-protection-act).
- Singtel's responsibilities are set by the contract and its data processing terms. The account executive never promises liability caps or indemnities; route the question to Legal through the deal room.
- Quote PDPA penalty amounts only from the PDPC source, never from memory.
- Position controls that reduce exposure: Unified SASE and Managed Security Services, and Quantum-Safe Network for long-lived sensitive data.

## "Your invoices do not match our new Oracle system"

- Acknowledge it and fix it before selling. A disputed invoice drops Paper Process to 0.
- Agree the Oracle supplier site code, one PO line per site, service credits as negative invoice lines, and one named billing contact on each side.
- Record the fix in a separate Chatter thread tagged with the invoice ID, such as SGT-INV-2026-8841.
- Never trade a billing fix for a commercial concession.

## "We already buy cloud from a hyperscaler reseller"

- Position RE:AI, Nxera, and CUBΣ as complementary: sovereign hosting for regulated workloads, and CUBΣ for visibility and control over the customer's digital infrastructure (source: https://www.singtel.com/business/products-services/connectivity/cube).

title: Outcome-based product mix
body:
Map each operational gap to an outcome bundle. Skip products the customer already owns; for owned products, propose an uplift instead of a new line. Indicative ARR is the sum of catalogue ARR for the products in the bundle; it is never Singtel list pricing.

## Unified SASE & SD-WAN + 5G

- Products: Cyber Security (SGT-CYBER), CUBΣ (SGT-CUBE), 5G+ (SGT-5G).
- What it delivers: Unified SASE convergence for edge-to-cloud connectivity and Managed Security Services (source: https://www.singtel.com/business/products-services/cybersecurity); one platform for enterprise networking including SD-WAN, network management, security, data, and AI (source: https://www.singtel.com/business/products-services/connectivity/cube); 5G with network slicing (source: https://www.singtel.com/business/products-services/5g).
- Gap signals: several sites with local internet breakout, partner tails, Wi-Fi congestion, or no single security policy.
- Indicative ARR: SGD 370,000.

## Private 5G + Edge

- Products: 5G+ (SGT-5G) with multi-access edge computing.
- What it delivers: low-latency applications processed at the edge, orchestrated through Paragon (source: https://www.singtel.com/business/products-services/5g).
- Gap signals: government, defence, or CII data residency terms; cranes, AGVs, or apron operations that need on-site processing.
- Indicative ARR: SGD 140,000.

## RE:AI sovereign AI + hyperscaler orchestration

- Products: RE:AI (SGT-REAI), Nxera (SGT-NXERA), CUBΣ (SGT-CUBE).
- What it delivers: GPU-as-a-Service on NVIDIA DGX GB300 and token-based AI services hosted in Singapore (source: https://www.re-ai.ai/about-us/newsroom/singtel-re-ai-first-in-APAC-to-deploy-nvidia-dgx-gb300); AI-ready colocation at DC Tuas with direct-to-chip liquid cooling (source: https://www.itnews.asia/news/singtels-nxera-opens-58mw-data-centre-in-singapore-623491); CUBΣ for visibility and control over the customer's digital infrastructure (source: https://www.singtel.com/business/products-services/connectivity/cube).
- Gap signals: GPU queues, AI models calling overseas endpoints, or contract terms that require in-country processing.
- Indicative ARR: SGD 620,000.

## Sequencing

1. Fix the pain with the highest measured cost first.
2. Offer a starter bundle when budget or the Economic Buyer is not confirmed.
3. Tie each bundle to one metric the customer named in MEDDPICC.

title: Chatter deal-room etiquette
body:
Each Opportunity's Chatter feed in Salesforce is its deal room. SingTech posts drafts there; people approve them.

## Rules

1. One thread per decision or request. Start with a one-line ask, then the context.
2. Mention specialists by desk (Connectivity, Cyber, Digital InfraCo, NCS) instead of broadcasting to everyone.
3. After each customer meeting, post the MEDDPICC change: element, old score, new score, and evidence.
4. Every claim about the customer links its source. No source, no claim.
5. Keep personal data out. Refer to customer people by role, and never post personal phone numbers, personal emails, or ID numbers. Text bound for Slack or Salesforce passes the redaction step first.
6. Post pricing only as indicative figures derived from catalogue ARR or as an approved quote reference. Never post Singtel list pricing.
7. Put billing disputes in their own thread tagged with the invoice ID (for example SGT-INV-2026-8841), so finance can follow without reading the deal thread.
8. Approvals are explicit: write "Approved" and name the item. A reaction is not an approval.
9. Use plain enterprise language: no emojis and no exclamation marks.
10. Close the loop: when an action is done, reply in its thread with the outcome and link the Salesforce Task.

## Post template

- Ask: what you need, from which desk.
- Account and Opportunity: name, Stage, and indicative ARR.
- Evidence: the measured strain, incident, or customer quote, with its source.
- Decision needed by: date.
